stem: Evaluation of teaching and learning is BEST described as which of the following?
options: The last phase of the teaching process, an ongoing appraisal of the patient's learning progress
A step that occurs only before teaching begins
A punitive measure with no relationship to learning outcomes
A process that has no bearing on instructional effectiveness

stem: Formative evaluation is used PRIMARILY to achieve which of the following?
options: Monitor the learning progress of students or clients during the period of instruction and provide continuous feedback
Assign a final grade at the end of a course only
Determine promotion to the next higher class exclusively
Certify that a learner has met externally determined standards only

stem: Which characteristic BEST describes formative evaluation?
options: It occurs frequently during the course of instruction and its results are made immediately known to learners
It occurs only once, at the very end of a course of instruction
It is judgmental in character and views evaluation as a product
It is used exclusively for promotion or certification purposes

stem: Which of the following is a recognized function of formative evaluation?
options: Diagnosing the most appropriate method or instructional materials conducive to learning
Assigning final grades at course completion
Selecting learners for further studies after course completion
Certifying that a learner meets previously determined external standards

stem: The 'monitoring' function of formative evaluation is concerned MOST with which of the following?
options: Keeping track of the day-to-day progress of learners and pointing out changes necessary in teaching strategies
Assigning a final course grade
Promoting a student to a higher class
Certifying achievement of predetermined standards

stem: The 'placement' function of formative evaluation is concerned MOST with which of the following?
options: Finding out the position of an individual in the curriculum from which he has to start learning
Determining a final examination score
Selecting learners for further studies after a course
Diagnosing appropriate instructional materials only

stem: Summative evaluation is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Evaluation done at the end of a course of instruction to ascertain the extent of accomplishment of set objectives
Evaluation done exclusively before instruction begins
A form of evaluation with no relationship to grading
A continuous process occurring only during instruction

stem: Which characteristic BEST distinguishes summative evaluation from formative evaluation?
options: Summative evaluation is judgmental in character because its chief concern is to point out the level of attainment
Summative evaluation occurs frequently throughout instruction with immediate feedback
Summative evaluation cannot be based on standardized tests
Summative evaluation is never used for grading purposes

stem: Which of the following is an example of a summative evaluation activity?
options: End of term or semester examination
Daily observation of a return demonstration
A single question asked mid-lecture
A quick checklist used during a single teaching session

stem: The 'crediting' function of summative evaluation is concerned MOST with which of the following?
options: Collecting evidence that a learner has achieved some instructional goals in contents with respect to a defined curricular programme
Determining the position of a learner in the curriculum before instruction begins
Monitoring day-to-day learner progress
Diagnosing instructional materials conducive to learning

stem: The 'certifying' function of summative evaluation is concerned MOST with which of the following?
options: Giving evidence that the learner is able to perform a job according to previously determined standards
Promoting a pupil to the next higher class
Selecting learners for further studies after completion of a course
Monitoring the day-to-day progress of a learner

stem: In client teaching, the teach-back method is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Confirming the patient's understanding of the information the care provider has imparted by having the patient explain it back in their own words
A method that assumes patient understanding without verification
A written examination administered only at hospital discharge
A method used exclusively to assess a nurse's own teaching skill and never the patient's understanding

stem: If a patient has trouble explaining or recalling material during teach-back, which nursing action is MOST appropriate?
options: Repeat, clarify, or modify the teaching and reassess the patient's understanding and recall, possibly over several cycles
Document that the patient understood and move on without further clarification
Discharge the patient regardless of comprehension
Avoid re-teaching because repetition confuses patients further

stem: Which of the following BEST reflects why the teach-back method 'is not a test' of the patient?
options: It re-enforces what was taught because the patient has to put the teaching into their own words, confirming the teacher's effectiveness rather than the patient's intelligence
It is designed to penalize patients who fail to recall information correctly
It assigns the patient a numerical grade for later reference
It replaces the need for any further nursing documentation

stem: The return demonstration method of evaluating client teaching is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Having the patient perform the skill that the nurse taught, enabling the nurse to evaluate how well the patient follows the correct steps
Having the patient answer only written multiple-choice questions
Having the nurse perform the skill while the patient watches passively with no participation
A method used only for evaluating community-wide health campaigns

stem: Measurement of behavioral change as an outcome goal of client teaching evaluation is BEST illustrated by which of the following examples?
options: A documented return of target blood glucose levels to normal over time as an indicator of successful diet teaching
A patient's self-reported satisfaction with the hospital food service
The number of pamphlets distributed to a patient
The length of time a teaching session lasted

stem: Documentation of client/patient teaching is BEST described as which of the following?
options: The manual or electronic recording of health education, the client's response, and the outcome of the teaching process
A verbal-only report given to the next shift with no written record
An optional step performed only if time permits
A record maintained exclusively by the patient's family

stem: Which of the following is a primary purpose of documenting patient teaching?
options: Promoting communication about the patient's progress among all members of the health care team and maintaining continuity of care
Providing entertainment reading material for the patient
Replacing the need for verbal communication among staff entirely
Avoiding the need for any further patient teaching sessions

stem: Which of the following pieces of information should a nurse include when documenting client teaching?
options: Date and time of teaching, topic/content taught, and teaching method used
The patient's unrelated personal opinions about hospital food
The nurse's personal schedule for the following week
Only the patient's insurance information

stem: Which of the following is a recommended guideline for HOW to document patient teaching?
options: Record the patient's name and include the time and date on all entries, and write legibly
Use pencil so entries can later be erased if needed
Record subjective personal bias about the patient
Leave entries unsigned to save time

stem: Which of the following is a recommended guideline for documenting patient teaching accurately?
options: Be accurate and truthful while discussing facts and events
Exaggerate outcomes to make the teaching appear more successful
Omit any details that reflect the patient's difficulty understanding
Record assumptions about the patient's future behavior with no evidence

stem: Community health education is BEST defined as which of the following?
options: The process of teaching individuals and populations how to improve, maintain, and restore their health
A process limited strictly to hospital inpatients
A process that excludes consideration of lifestyle factors
A one-time lecture with no follow-up evaluation

stem: A Community Health Education program is targeted MOST at positively influencing which of the following?
options: The health behavior of individuals, families, and groups in the communities
Only the health behavior of hospital employees
Only the profitability of local pharmacies
Only the architectural design of clinics

stem: Which of the following is the FIRST step in the community health education process?
options: Assessment
Diagnosis
Planning
Evaluation

stem: During the assessment step of community health education, the nurse should do which of the following?
options: Collect data on the community's demographics, health status, and resources
Design the program layout and timelines exclusively
Deliver the educational program using verbal communication only
Measure whether the community met the set objectives

stem: During the diagnosis step of community health education, the nurse should do which of the following?
options: Analyze the collected data to pinpoint specific community health problems
Distribute educational materials to community members
Gather data on community demographics for the first time
Revise future teaching sessions based on program results

stem: During the planning step of community health education, the nurse should do which of the following?
options: Establish clear, measurable short-term and long-term learning objectives
Analyze collected data to identify community health problems for the first time
Deliver the educational program to the community
Gather feedback from community members after program delivery

stem: During the implementation step of community health education, the nurse should do which of the following?
options: Deliver the educational program using clear verbal and non-verbal communication and encourage active participation
Collect demographic data on the community for the first time
Formulate community nursing diagnoses for the first time
Revise the program timeline before any data collection

stem: During the evaluation step of community health education, the nurse should do which of the following?
options: Measure whether the community met the set objectives and gained knowledge
Collect initial demographic data on the community
Formulate nursing diagnoses that target knowledge deficits
Design the program layout and assign responsibilities for the first time

stem: Which of the following is a teaching method commonly utilized in community health education?
options: Health talks, group discussion, demonstration, role play, and drama
Only individual bedside teaching with no group methods
Exclusively written multiple-choice examinations
Only computer-based instruction with no in-person contact

stem: Group teaching in nursing education is BEST described as which of the following?
options: An instructional approach that involves learners working together in groups of 5 to 10 and increases student retention, teamwork ability, communication skills, and peer-peer interaction
A method restricted to individual, one-on-one instruction only
A method that discourages any peer interaction
A method used exclusively for summative testing

stem: The model of group teaching commonly referenced in nursing education, developed to establish small group teaching sessions, is associated with which name?
options: Tuckman's model
Maslow's model
Piaget's model
Thorndike's model

stem: In Tuckman's group development model, the 'Forming' stage is BEST characterized by which of the following?
options: Members of the team know each other, exchange information, and understand how they respond
Identification of the topic or problem to be solved
Institution of specific aims, objectives, and a mutual plan
The team functions to implement the plan

stem: In Tuckman's group development model, the 'Storming' stage is BEST characterized by which of the following?
options: Identification of the topic or problem to be solved
Members getting to know each other for the first time
The team functioning to implement an agreed plan
Institution of specific aims and a mutual plan

stem: In Tuckman's group development model, the 'Norming' stage is BEST characterized by which of the following?
options: Institution of specific aims, objectives, and a mutual plan
Members getting to know each other for the first time
Identification of the topic or problem to be solved
The team functioning to implement the plan

stem: In Tuckman's group development model, the 'Performing' stage is BEST characterized by which of the following?
options: The team functions to implement the plan
Members getting to know each other for the first time
Identification of the topic or problem to be solved
Institution of specific aims and objectives only

stem: Which of the following is a recognized advantage of group teaching?
options: It facilitates sharing of knowledge and skills and provides opportunity for exchange of information
It guarantees equal participation from every member with no risk of imbalance
It eliminates the need for a facilitator entirely
It removes any possibility of conflict among members

stem: Which of the following is a recognized disadvantage of group teaching?
options: There may be unequal support from the instructor and conflict over roles and responsibilities may arise
It always produces perfectly equal participation among all members
It requires no debriefing or evaluation at the end of the session
It guarantees improved outcomes with no risk of unequal participation

stem: The problem-solving method of teaching is BEST described as which of the following?
options: A learner-centered approach in which students are presented with real-world problems and encouraged to use their own knowledge and skills to come up with solutions
A method in which the teacher provides the only correct answer with no learner input
A method that discourages critical thinking
A method used exclusively for summative examinations

stem: Which of the following is a recognized benefit of the problem-solving method of teaching?
options: It enhances critical thinking by forcing students to think critically about a situation and come up with their own solutions
It removes any need for creativity
It discourages real-world application of knowledge
It guarantees a single correct answer for every problem presented

stem: Which of the following BEST describes how the problem-solving method fosters creativity?
options: There is often no one right answer, so students are free to come up with unique solutions
It requires students to memorize a single fixed solution
It eliminates the need for critical thinking entirely
It restricts students to only one predetermined method of solving a problem

stem: Which of the following is the FIRST step in the problem-solving method of teaching?
options: Identifying the problem
Generating possible solutions
Implementing the solution
Evaluating the results

stem: During the 'understanding the problem' step of the problem-solving method, students should do which of the following?
options: Break the problem down into smaller parts and gather more information about the problem
Immediately implement a solution with no analysis
Skip directly to evaluating results
Avoid gathering any additional information

stem: During the 'generating possible solutions' step of the problem-solving method, students may use which of the following techniques?
options: Brainstorming or problem-solving techniques such as root cause analysis or the decision matrix
Immediate implementation with no solution generation
Skipping directly to evaluation with no plan developed
Avoiding any analysis of the problem

stem: If a chosen solution is not successful during the problem-solving method of teaching, students should do which of the following?
options: Go back to step 3 (generating possible solutions) and develop new solutions
Abandon the problem entirely with no further attempt
Immediately conclude that the method has failed permanently
Repeat the exact same unsuccessful solution without modification

stem: Behavior modification instructional method is BEST described as which of the following?
options: An approach that tries to change the pattern of human behavior by using various motivated techniques such as reinforcement, extinction, fading, shaping, and chaining
A method that relies exclusively on lecture with no behavioral techniques
A method that has no basis in behavioral research
A method used only in classroom settings with no clinical application

stem: Which of the following BEST defines reinforcement in behavior modification?
options: Anything that increases the likelihood that a learner will repeat a behavior
Anything that decreases the likelihood a behavior will occur again
The complete removal of a behavior from the learner's repertoire
A punishment applied to discourage a behavior

stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of reinforcement decreasing the chance an action or behavior will be repeated, according to behaviorist principles?
options: If the consequences of an action or behavior are unfavorable
If the consequences of an action or behavior are favorable
If the behavior is ignored entirely with no consequence
If the behavior is paired with an unrelated neutral stimulus

stem: Extinction in behavior modification is BEST described as which of the following?
options: A behavior becomes extinct when a stimulus or reinforcer is removed
A behavior that is strengthened through repeated reinforcement
A behavior that occurs only once and is never repeated regardless of consequence
A behavior that is punished harshly to increase its frequency

stem: Which of the following is the BEST clinical example of extinction as described in behavior modification?
options: A hysteric patient who was accustomed to getting a bottle of soft drink if he discovers the giver stopped providing it and no longer displays vomiting to obtain a soft drink, the behavior eventually becomes extinct
A patient who receives verbal praise every time sterile technique is performed correctly and repeats the behavior more often
A child who is gradually reinforced with small steps toward walking independently
A patient who follows several stages of wound dressing taught in sequence

stem: Shaping in behavior modification is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Reinforcing behaviors that are closer to a desired behavior than the current disposition
Removing all reinforcement to eliminate a behavior entirely
Teaching an entire complex task in a single step with no incremental reinforcement
Punishing every attempt until the desired behavior spontaneously appears

stem: Which of the following is the BEST clinical example of shaping in behavior modification?
options: A child learning to walk is reinforced through several stages such as sitting, crowing, standing, and walking, with the parent reinforcing each new step
A patient stops vomiting once a reinforcing soft drink is withdrawn
A parent rewards a child with money for good grades and later replaces the reward with praise
Gathering equipment and skin preparation are taught separately before the main procedure

stem: Fading, as a behavior modification technique, is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Gradually shifting from one stimulus to another, such as replacing an old stimulus with a new one that reflects a desired outcome
Immediately withdrawing all forms of reinforcement with no gradual transition
Punishing a behavior repeatedly until it disappears entirely
Teaching an entire behavior chain in a single uninterrupted step

stem: Which of the following is the BEST clinical example of fading in behavior modification?
options: A parent rewards a child's good grades with money and gradually seeks to find a more sustainable stimulus, such as praise, to replace the money
A patient's vomiting behavior becomes extinct once the reinforcing drink is withdrawn
A child is reinforced through the stages of sitting, crawling, and walking
A complex behavior is broken down into simplest steps for easier achievement

stem: Behavior chaining, as a behavior modification technique, is BEST described as which of the following?
options: Breaking down a complex task into its simplest steps to make the behavior more consistently achievable
Removing a behavior from a learner's repertoire entirely with no incremental steps
Reinforcing every step of a task identically with no sequential structure
Gradually replacing one stimulus with another unrelated stimulus

stem: Which of the following is the BEST clinical example of behavior chaining in nursing education?
options: Activities involved in teaching insulin administration, such as gathering equipment and skin preparation, are taught separately and followed by the main procedure
A hysteric patient's vomiting behavior becomes extinct after a reinforcing drink is withdrawn
A parent replaces a monetary reward with verbal praise for good grades
A child is reinforced through successive approximations of walking

stem: Trans-cultural teaching is a style of teaching that aims MOST to achieve which of the following?
options: Engaging learners from different cultures and knowledge traditions in a way that respects differences, acknowledges a common goal, and seeks to co-create new knowledge
Ignoring cultural differences entirely to maintain a single standardized approach
Excluding learners whose culture differs from the teacher's own background
Focusing exclusively on the teacher's own cultural traditions with no learner input

stem: Which of the following is a recognized element of a culturally inclusive teaching plan?
options: Gather demographic information on students' or clients' background and language spoken
Avoid any acknowledgment of a student's cultural background
Exclude cultural traditions or holidays from classroom activities entirely
Assume the teacher's own personal biases are universally shared

stem: Culturally responsive teaching attempts to bridge the gap between teacher and student by helping the teacher understand which of the following?
options: Cultural differences that may cause a relationship to break down which ultimately affects student achievement
Only the teacher's own personal preferences
The financial background of the institution with no reference to the learner
Standardized test scores exclusively

stem: Computer-assisted instruction (CAI) is BEST defined as which of the following?
options: Any teaching-learning activity or remediation presented on a computer to enhance student understanding or facilitate learning and improve instructional qualities
A method that requires no computer or digital device whatsoever
A method used exclusively for grading with no instructional content
A method restricted only to community health settings

stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of an effective teacher?
options: Having adequate skills about the teaching/learning process and broad knowledge of the content of the curriculum
Frequently losing temper in class to maintain discipline
Avoiding the use of any board or teaching aids
Maintaining a distant, unfriendly relationship with learners

stem: Which of the following BEST reflects a recognized rule for teaching a lesson effectively?
options: Teaching a lesson proceeds from the known to the unknown and from the simple to the complex
Teaching a lesson should proceed from the unfamiliar to the familiar with no prior grounding
Teaching a lesson should proceed from abstract to concrete exclusively with no concrete grounding
Teaching a lesson should proceed from complex to simple exclusively

stem: Which of the following BEST reflects the 'whole to parts' rule of teaching?
options: Presenting an overview before details
Presenting details before any overview is given
Presenting only isolated facts with no overview at all
Avoiding any structured sequence in a lesson

stem: Which of the following BEST reflects the 'concrete to abstract' rule of teaching?
options: Beginning instruction with tangible examples before introducing abstract concepts
Beginning instruction with abstract theory before any concrete example
Avoiding concrete examples entirely throughout instruction
Presenting abstract and concrete content in no particular order

stem: Which of the following factors is recognized as affecting the teaching and learning process?
options: Maturity, age, motivation, previous learning, intelligence, mental health, physical need, diet and nutrition, and attention and interest
Only the color of the classroom walls
Only the brand of writing materials used
Only the time of day with no other contributing factor

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A nurse teaches a patient about insulin self-injection, then asks the patient to explain the procedure back in their own words. The patient describes the steps but omits checking the expiration date. The nurse re-explains this single point and asks the patient to repeat the explanation again. Which evaluation method is being used, and is this method a test of the patient?
options: Teach-back method; it is not a test of the patient but a check of the effectiveness of the teaching
Return demonstration method; it is a graded test of the patient's manual dexterity
Summative evaluation; it assigns the patient a final course grade
Formative evaluation; it is used only for placement purposes

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A community health nurse collects demographic data, health status information, and identifies learning gaps in a rural community, then prioritizes health problems based on urgency and severity before designing an educational program with clear objectives. Which two steps of the community health education process are being demonstrated in this sequence?
options: Assessment followed by diagnosis
Implementation followed by evaluation
Evaluation followed by assessment
Diagnosis followed by assessment

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A hysteric client was accustomed to receiving a bottle of soft drink whenever she vomited. Once her family stops giving her the drink in response to vomiting, the vomiting behavior gradually stops occurring. Which behavior modification principle is BEST demonstrated?
options: Extinction, because removal of the reinforcer caused the behavior to stop
Shaping, because the behavior was reinforced in successive steps
Fading, because one stimulus was gradually replaced by another
Chaining, because a complex task was broken into simple steps

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A nurse educator organizes a class of 40 nursing students into groups of 8 to discuss a complex case study. Initially the group members introduce themselves and exchange background information, then disagreements arise over which approach to the case is correct, followed eventually by the group agreeing on a shared plan and completing the assignment together. Which of Tuckman's stages have been demonstrated, in order?
options: Forming, Storming, Norming, and Performing
Performing, Norming, Storming, and Forming
Storming, Forming, Performing, and Norming
Norming, Performing, Forming, and Storming

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A nurse teaching insulin administration to a new diabetic patient first teaches the patient to gather supplies and clean the injection site as a separate step, then teaches drawing up the correct dose separately, and finally combines both into the complete procedure. Which behavior modification technique is BEST demonstrated?
options: Behavior chaining
Extinction
Fading
Classical conditioning

___ evaluation is done at the end of a course of instruction to ascertain the extent of accomplishment of set objectives.
The diagnosing function of formative evaluation is concerned with determining the most appropriate method or instructional ___ conducive to learning.
The placement function of formative evaluation finds out the ___ of an individual in the curriculum from which he has to start learning.
The crediting function of summative evaluation is concerned with collecting evidence that a learner has achieved instructional ___.
The certifying function of summative evaluation gives evidence that the learner is able to perform a job according to previously determined ___.
The teach-back method confirms the patient's ___ of the information the care provider has imparted.
In teach-back, if a patient has trouble explaining the material, the nurse should repeat, clarify, or ___ the teaching.
The ___ demonstration method has the patient perform the skill taught to evaluate how well the patient follows correct steps.
Documentation of client teaching promotes ___ about the patient's progress among all health care team members.
Good documentation of patient teaching helps maintain continuity of care and avoids ___ of teaching.
When documenting patient teaching, the nurse should record the date and ___ of the teaching.
When documenting patient teaching, the nurse should be accurate and ___ while discussing facts and events.
Community health education is the process of teaching individuals and populations how to improve, maintain, and ___ their health.
The first step in the community health education process is ___.
During the diagnosis step of community health education, the nurse formulates community nursing ___ that target knowledge or behavior deficits.
During the planning step of community health education, the nurse establishes clear, measurable short-term and long-term learning ___.
Group teaching in nursing education typically involves learners working together in groups of ___ to 10.
The model of group teaching commonly established in small group teaching sessions was developed by ___.
In Tuckman's model, the ___ stage involves members getting to know each other and exchanging information.
In Tuckman's model, the ___ stage involves identification of the topic or problem to be solved.
___ , at the end of a group teaching session, summarizes and clarifies what has been learnt.
The problem-solving method of teaching is a ___-centered approach to learning.
The first step of the problem-solving method of teaching is identifying the ___.
In behavior modification, ___ is anything that increases the likelihood that a learner will repeat a behavior.
A behavior becomes ___ when a stimulus or reinforcer is removed and the behavior stops occurring.
___ involves reinforcing behaviors that are closer to a desired behavior than the current disposition.
